shortDescription: Chicago Board of Trade wheat futures fell as traders focused on the impacts of Russia's war on Ukraine, with renewed diplomatic moves to end the war adding bearishness.

children: Chicago Board of Trade wheat futures fell as traders focused on the impacts of Russia's war on Ukraine, with renewed diplomatic moves to end the war adding bearishness.
Attacks on the city of Dnipro that damaged a vegetable oil factory of U.S. agrifood group Bunge
kept attention on continuing disruption to the massive Black Sea grain trade.
Commerzbank raised its year-end wheat price forecasts, citing the ongoing attacks by Russia and Ukraine on each other's ports.

Russia's seaborne grain exports fell by 61.9% year-on-year in August to 2.0 million metric tons, mainly due to a decline in shipments through the Azov-Black Sea basin, according to shipping data from industry sources released on Friday.

Russia and Ukraine have sharply escalated attacks on each other's shipping in recent weeks. Following drone strikes, Russian authorities suspended navigation in the Sea of Azov in early July, while an August 12 attack halted loading operations at key terminals at Novorossiysk, Russia's largest Black Sea port.
Exports via Azov and Black Sea ports declined by 73.1% year-on-year in August to 1.3 million tons, the data showed.
CBOT December soft red winter wheat (WZ26) settled 12-1/2 cents lower to $7.41-1/4 per bushel.
Kansas City December hard red winter wheat (KWZ26) settled 20-1/4 cents lower to $7.98-1/2 per bushel.
Minneapolis December wheat (MWEZ26) settled 17-1/2 cents lower to $7.45 per bushel.
